source.quote: Shanling's own manual for the UA6 II, UA6II.pdf, read 2026-11-25 - the product page is image-only, so the manual is the source. Its numbered feature list: « 1. True Octuple DAC setup with Cirrus Logic CD43131 DACs. » « 2. Hi-Res PCM support up to 32bit / 768kHz. » « 3. Native DSD support up to DSD512. » Menu settings: Filter.

facts.chip: « True Octuple DAC setup with Cirrus Logic CD43131 DACs » in the manual; the announcement at /article/101201 writes « 8x DAC Assembly - 8x Cirrus Logic CS43131 DACs ». Both forms quoted.

device_settings.why: « Filter (0-4) », options « Fast Roll-Off / Slow Roll-Off / Low-Latency Fast / Low-Latency Slow / NOS » - five positions, all five named, the fifth being non-oversampling. The UA6 II has no valves, so NOS is unambiguous, and selecting it takes the interpolation filter out of the path. The only `correctable` USB dongle in the catalogue.

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_le_mot_NATIF_vient_du_manuel_et_nest_pa: « Native DSD support up to DSDnnn » is the manual's own wording, in a numbered feature list, and it appears in every UA manual in the same form. It is NOT the boilerplate that had to be refused on xDuoo, where one sentence was repeated on twenty unrelated pages including a passive module: here it sits on a family of dongles whose only digital input is the USB-C port it describes, and the figure varies by model - DSD256 on the UA1 Plus and UA1s, DSD512 on the rest. A claim that varies with the product is a claim about the product. DoP is never mentioned for any UA model.
_le_SEUL_dongle_du_catalogue_qui_sait_ne: Eight converters in a stick the size of a lighter, and a menu position that turns the digital filter off. `correctable` has until now belonged to desktop ladders and high-end machines; this is the first device under 100 grams to carry it. Its own sibling the UA6 has the same five-position menu with the positions NUMBERED instead of named, so whether the UA6's fifth position is also NOS cannot be established - and is not guessed.
